implementation.summary: D45 fixes KafkaJsonSource so a bounded poll retries transient empty/partition-EOF results within the configured timeout and can discover records from a later assigned partition without exceeding record or batch byte limits. A real backlog test also captures its API traffic for candidate-bound audit.

security_and_recovery.journey: The exact live journey created the sustained two-partition stream, confirmed 32/32 initial lag, repeatedly executed real bounded Kafka micro-batches, checked health after each run, consumed all 64 rows and cleaned the isolated PostgreSQL/Redpanda services.
security_and_recovery.negative_paths: The unit regression preserves the bounded timeout and later-partition behavior; no invalid or poison record path was claimed by D45. The prior live attempt that stalled at the 40-attempt cap is retained as failure evidence.
security_and_recovery.recovery_scope: This campaign proves bounded multi-partition backlog drain and transient poll recovery. It does not prove broker restart recovery beyond D44, sustained indefinite backpressure, worker supervision, external provider breadth or the complete P11 journey.

limitations: The first candidate-bound live attempt on a12616ee captured 82 successful API events but reached the 40-attempt cap without lag zero; it is recorded as FAIL and led to the transient empty-poll correction.
D45 proves one bounded local two-partition backlog scenario and does not prove indefinite load, multi-broker quorum recovery, worker supervision, external providers or the full P11 family journey.
